data.title: How Do 3 ETFs Change Your JPMorgan Chase Risk?

Owning JPMorgan Chase inside a fund that also holds other companies limits how much any single problem or success moves your overall portfolio, and also trims the upside from one winner.

For investors who want the banking giant as part of a wider basket, XLF, MGV and VFH are three ETF tickers that include the stock among broader holdings.

State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF)

A risk for JPMorgan Chase is that spending on marketing, technology and AI could climb faster than revenue and weigh on margins. XLF holds other financial industries such as insurance, asset management and exchanges, which do not rely on the same expense decisions at the bank, so that pressure is partly isolated to JPMorgan Chase. If that tone cools across financials, banks inside MGV could all feel it, while semiconductor, healthcare and energy holdings depend more on chip demand, drug markets and global energy conditions instead.
